findings.reason: The protected Python solution finds the nearest right node to a target node u at the same level in a binary tree using breadth-first search (BFS). It processes nodes level by level using a queue and level_size boundary. When node is u, if it is not the last node in the current level, it returns queue[0]; otherwise it returns None. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(w) space where w is max level width; no candidate is required.
Tracking level_size ensures same-level nodes are distinguished from newly queued children of the next level. Identity comparison node is u accurately identifies target node.
Visiting each node at most once takes O(n) time. Queue holds at most one level's width w plus children, taking O(w) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts root and target node u, returning the nearest right TreeNode object at the same depth level or None.

The approach accurately details BFS level-by-level processing, same-level queue inspection, target object identity comparison, and O(n) time / O(w) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover storing full level lists extra allocations, repeated root-to-node search quadratic costs, node value comparison pitfalls, root node level zero handling, cross-parent right neighbors, and queue child isolation.
